text:
Jack Roslovic, on his sixth NHL team, has become one of the Maple Leafs' few reliable sources of offense: 20 points in 21 games, nine goals, and a run CBS Sports noted of points in eight of nine games. Our wins-added numbers rank him 22nd of 530 skaters, because his goals have tended to come when they swing games.

The finishing is the part to hold loosely. Nine goals on 5.7 expected, shooting about 16%, is above anything his talent range supports, and he has gone pointless in his last two games as Toronto lost five straight. The underlying work is good, though: the Leafs control 51.4% of expected goals at 5v5 with him on, and he is 7.44 points better than the team when he sits.

What makes him interesting is speed. His top skating speed is in the 99th percentile and he has 75 bursts over 20 mph. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 54% of his shots coming off the rush last season. On a team searching for answers, the Columbus native playing 18 to 21 minutes a night is one of the ones that has worked.
headline: Jack Roslovic is scoring for a team that isn't
